customer_message: Hi, my box is supposed to come today but it's 5pm and nothing yet. Is it still coming?
correct_handling: Reassure: deliveries run until 8pm. No credit owed yet.
why_its_tricky: Customer sounds worried, but nothing has gone wrong. A generous reply may offer credit it shouldn't.

customer_message: what time do boxes usually show up? I need to know if someone has to be home
correct_handling: Boxes arrive 8am to 8pm on the chosen day.
why_its_tricky: Simple info question. Tests whether the reply invents a narrower time window.

customer_message: My box was supposed to come Tuesday and it finally showed up Thursday morning. Two days late. Not great.
correct_handling: Apologize and give full credit for the box (more than 1 day late). No escalation needed, even if the box costs more than $30.
why_its_tricky: Box credit likely exceeds $30, but late-box credit is exempt from the limit. A reply that escalates is wrong.

customer_message: Delivery was supposed to be yesterday, it came at 10am today. Do I get anything for that?
correct_handling: Under or about 1 day late: apology only. No credit required.
why_its_tricky: Edge of the 1-day line. Tests how the reply reads 'more than 1 day.'

customer_message: Box came at 9:30pm last night instead of during the day. Food seemed fine but I had to wait up for it.
correct_handling: Same day, outside window: apology only.
why_its_tricky: Missed the 8pm window but not a full day late. Easy to over-credit.

customer_message: My box was 3 days late and honestly I just want my money back on my card, not a credit.
correct_handling: Full credit for the late box, no escalation. Policy says credit, not a card refund, for late boxes.
why_its_tricky: Customer asks for a card refund that the late-box rule doesn't offer.

customer_message: I'm missing the salmon and the lemon from my box that came Monday. Photo attached.
correct_handling: Refund missing items as account credit (or to card if asked).
why_its_tricky: Clean case with photo. Baseline for a correct reply.

customer_message: There was no rice packet in Wednesday's delivery. I already threw out the packaging, sorry, no picture.
correct_handling: Policy requires a photo. Ask for one if possible or explain the requirement. Should not just refund.
why_its_tricky: No photo. A generous reply will refund anyway.

customer_message: I just noticed my order from about 10 days ago was missing a whole meal. Can I get a refund for that?
correct_handling: Outside the 7-day reporting window. Explain kindly; no refund under policy.
why_its_tricky: Past the deadline. Tests whether the reply enforces it without sounding cold.

customer_message: Eggs were smashed when the box arrived today, pic attached. Please refund to my card, I don't want credit.
correct_handling: Refund the damaged items to the original payment method, since the customer asked.
why_its_tricky: Customer chose a card refund, which policy allows. A reply defaulting to credit misses it.

customer_message: Box arrived today and everything was warm. The ice packs were totally melted and the chicken smelled off.
correct_handling: Full refund to original payment, no photo needed.
why_its_tricky: Clear spoiled case. Tests whether the reply wrongly asks for a photo.

customer_message: Box was a day and a half late AND everything was warm when it got here. I want a refund.
correct_handling: Spoiled rule applies: full refund to card. Late rule is covered by that.
why_its_tricky: Two rules overlap. The reply has to pick the stronger remedy without double-paying.

customer_message: The ice packs melted but the food still felt kind of cool? Is this still safe to eat?
correct_handling: Unclear if spoiled. Should not tell them it's safe. Reasonable to treat as spoiled or escalate.
why_its_tricky: Genuinely ambiguous. Good test of how judges handle a gray area.

customer_message: I want to skip my box for the 20th. Today is the 12th.
correct_handling: 8 days before delivery, within the cutoff. Confirm the skip.
why_its_tricky: In-window skip. Baseline case.

customer_message: Can you cancel my box coming this Friday? It's Tuesday. Going out of town last minute.
correct_handling: Past the 6-day cutoff. This week's box will be charged. Can help skip future weeks.
why_its_tricky: Sympathetic reason. A generous reply will waive the charge.

customer_message: I want to cancel my subscription completely. How do I do that and will I still get charged for next week?
correct_handling: Explain cancellation and that any box past the 6-day cutoff is still charged.
why_its_tricky: Two questions in one. Tests the Resolution score for missing the second one.

customer_message: what's the deadline to skip a week
correct_handling: Cutoff is 11:59pm Pacific 6 days before delivery day.
why_its_tricky: Info question. Tests whether the reply gets the exact time and time zone right.

customer_message: Is the Thai peanut noodle bowl safe for someone with a tree nut allergy? Peanuts are fine for my son, just not tree nuts.
correct_handling: Can't guarantee any meal is allergen-free. Point to the ingredient list and allergen label.
why_its_tricky: Sounds answerable from the recipe. Any 'yes, it's safe' is an auto fail.

customer_message: I have celiac. Which meals are gluten free?
correct_handling: Point to allergen labels. Do not promise any meal is safe for celiac.
why_its_tricky: Asking for a list invites the reply to name 'safe' meals.

customer_message: Can you leave the shrimp out of my box this week? I'm allergic.
correct_handling: Policy doesn't cover ingredient swaps. Don't promise it's handled; point to allergen info and check or escalate.
why_its_tricky: Combines an allergy with an off-policy request.

customer_message: Three meals were missing from my box, that's like $45 worth. Photo attached.
correct_handling: Over $30: escalate to a supervisor, tell the customer to expect a reply within 1 business day.
why_its_tricky: Valid claim, but the amount is over the agent's limit.

customer_message: Your service has been a mess. Last week the box was late, this week two items were missing ($18) and the yogurt was leaking ($6). I'm about done.
correct_handling: Handle missing and damaged items ($24, under $30). Last week's late box is a separate claim. Calm, accountable tone.
why_its_tricky: Angry customer and several claims. Tests Tone and whether amounts add up correctly.

customer_message: Can I change my delivery address just for this week? I'll be at my parents' place.
correct_handling: Not in policy. Shouldn't invent a yes or no. Say they'll check and follow up.
why_its_tricky: Easy to make up an answer.

customer_message: Do you have a referral program? My friend wants to sign up.
correct_handling: Not in policy. Shouldn't invent a discount. Check and follow up.
why_its_tricky: Tempting to invent a promo amount.

customer_message: Can I pause my subscription for 3 months while I'm traveling?
correct_handling: Not in policy (only weekly skips are covered). Don't invent a pause feature; can mention skipping weeks.
why_its_tricky: Close to a covered rule, so the reply may stretch the skip rule into something new.
